items.readable_text:
Content:
To divide two fractions, we multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction.

Content:
As an example, let's consider the following division problem:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{3}{4}\div\dfrac{2}{5}]

Content:
The second fraction is [MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}5},] and the reciprocal of this fraction is [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{blue}2}.] So, we have

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac 3 4 \div \dfrac{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}5} = \dfrac 3 4 \times \dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{blue}2} .]

Content:
Now, we multiply fractions. We multiply the numerators, and we multiply the denominators:
[MATH: \dfrac 3 {4} \times \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac {3 \times 5} {4 \times 2} = \dfrac{15}{8}]

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{3}{4}\div\dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{15}{8}.]

items.title: Dividing Unit Fractions

sections.normalized_html:
Dividing a fraction by another fraction is equivalent to multiplying the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction.

The reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}1}{\color{red}8}] is [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}8}{\color{blue}1}.] So, we have: [MATH: \dfrac 1 4 \div \dfrac{\color{blue}1}{\color{red}8} = \dfrac 1 4 \times \dfrac{\color{red}8}{\color{blue}1}]

Now, we multiply fractions. We multiply the numerators, and we multiply the denominators: [MATH: \dfrac 1 {4} \times \dfrac{8}{1} = \dfrac {1\times 8} {4\times 1} = \dfrac{8}{4}]

Finally, we simplify: [MATH: 8\div 4=2]

Therefore, [MATH: \dfrac{1}{4} \div \dfrac{1}{8} = 2 \, .]

sections.normalized_html:
Dividing a fraction by another fraction is equivalent to multiplying the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second fraction.

The reciprocal of [MATH: \dfrac{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}13}] is [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}13}{\color{blue}2}.] So, we have [MATH: \dfrac 1 {3} \div \dfrac{\color{blue}2}{\color{red}13} = \dfrac 1 {3} \times \dfrac{\color{red}13}{\color{blue}2}.]

Now, we multiply fractions. We multiply the numerators, and we multiply the denominators: [MATH: \dfrac 1 {3} \times \dfrac{13}{2} = \dfrac {1\times 13} {3 \times 2} = \dfrac{13}{6}]

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number: [MATH: \dfrac{13}{6} =2\,\textrm{R} 1 = 2\,\dfrac 1 {6}]

Therefore, [MATH: \dfrac{1}{3} \div \dfrac 2 {13} = 2\,\dfrac 1 {6} \, .]
